checks.title: Key Vault restricts access to private networks

guardrails.recommendation: Enable secure transfer (supportsHttpsTrafficOnly: true) so the account only accepts HTTPS requests.
guardrails.risk: Plain HTTP requests expose data and shared keys to interception in transit.
guardrails.policy: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled

guardrails.recommendation: Disable anonymous public blob access (allowBlobPublicAccess: false) on the account.
guardrails.risk: Anonymous containers let anyone on the internet list and read blob data.
guardrails.policy: Storage account public access should be disallowed

guardrails.recommendation: Disable public network access and set networkAcls defaultAction to 'Deny'; reach the account through a private endpoint or selected virtual networks, allowing trusted Microsoft services.
guardrails.risk: A storage endpoint reachable from any network widens the attack surface for credential stuffing and data exfiltration.
guardrails.policy: Storage accounts should disable public network access

guardrails.recommendation: Require TLS 1.2 or later (minimumTlsVersion: 'TLS1_2').
guardrails.risk: Legacy TLS 1.0/1.1 protocols have known weaknesses that allow downgrade and decryption attacks.
guardrails.policy: Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version

guardrails.recommendation: Keep storage service encryption (SSE) for encryption at rest enabled; use customer-managed keys in Key Vault when regulation requires key custody.
guardrails.risk: Without controlled encryption at rest, compromised media or backups could expose data.
guardrails.policy: Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption

guardrails.recommendation: Disable shared key authorization (allowSharedKeyAccess: false) and use Microsoft Entra ID with RBAC for data access.
guardrails.risk: Account keys grant full, non-attributable access and are frequently leaked in code and config.
guardrails.policy: Storage accounts should prevent shared key access

guardrails.recommendation: Enable blob and container soft delete with a retention period of at least 7 days.
guardrails.risk: Accidental or malicious deletion becomes unrecoverable.
guardrails.policy: Soft delete should be enabled for blobs and containers

guardrails.recommendation: Enable purge protection (enablePurgeProtection: true) so deleted vaults and secrets cannot be permanently purged during the retention period.
guardrails.risk: An attacker or mistake could permanently destroy keys, making encrypted data unrecoverable.
guardrails.policy: Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled

guardrails.recommendation: Restrict the vault to private networks: publicNetworkAccess 'Disabled' with a private link endpoint, or networkAcls defaultAction 'Deny' with trusted service bypass.
guardrails.risk: A vault reachable from the public internet is exposed to brute-force and token replay attempts.
guardrails.policy: Azure Key Vault should disable public network access

guardrails.recommendation: Keep soft delete enabled with softDeleteRetentionInDays set (90 recommended).
guardrails.risk: Deleted secrets, keys and certificates cannot be recovered.
guardrails.policy: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled

guardrails.recommendation: Use the Azure RBAC permission model (enableRbacAuthorization: true) instead of vault access policies.
guardrails.risk: Access policies are coarse-grained and bypass central RBAC governance and PIM.
guardrails.policy: Azure Key Vault should use RBAC permission model

guardrails.recommendation: Send AuditEvent logs to a Log Analytics workspace through diagnostic settings.
guardrails.risk: Secret access cannot be investigated after an incident.
guardrails.policy: Resource logs in Key Vault should be enabled

guardrails.recommendation: Set expiration dates on secrets and keys and rotate them before expiry.
guardrails.risk: Long-lived secrets increase the blast radius of a leak.
guardrails.policy: Key Vault secrets should have an expiration date

guardrails.recommendation: Set httpsOnly: true on the function app.
guardrails.risk: Function triggers over HTTP expose payloads and function keys.
guardrails.policy: Function apps should only be accessible over HTTPS

guardrails.recommendation: Disable public network access for internal functions and integrate the app with a virtual network.
guardrails.risk: Publicly reachable function endpoints can be invoked or abused by anyone holding a leaked key.
guardrails.policy: Function apps should disable public network access

guardrails.recommendation: Set httpsOnly: true so HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.
guardrails.risk: Traffic over plain HTTP can be intercepted or modified.
guardrails.policy: App Service apps should only be accessible over HTTPS

guardrails.recommendation: Disable public network access for internal apps and front them with a private endpoint, Application Gateway or Front Door.
guardrails.risk: Internal workloads exposed to the internet invite scanning and exploitation.
guardrails.policy: App Service apps should disable public network access

guardrails.recommendation: Require TLS 1.2 or later (siteConfig.minTlsVersion: '1.2').
guardrails.risk: Older TLS versions are vulnerable to protocol downgrade attacks.
guardrails.policy: Function apps should use the latest TLS version

guardrails.recommendation: Use a managed identity for the AzureWebJobsStorage connection and downstream services (identity-based connections).
guardrails.risk: Storage account keys in app settings grant full account access if leaked.
guardrails.policy: Function apps should use managed identity

guardrails.recommendation: Require TLS 1.2 or later (siteConfig.minTlsVersion: '1.2').
guardrails.risk: Older TLS versions are vulnerable to protocol downgrade attacks.
guardrails.policy: App Service apps should use the latest TLS version

guardrails.recommendation: Enable a managed identity and use it to reach Key Vault, Storage and databases instead of connection strings.
guardrails.risk: Embedded credentials leak through app settings, logs and source control.
guardrails.policy: App Service apps should use managed identity

guardrails.recommendation: Disable FTP deployment (siteConfig.ftpsState: 'Disabled' or 'FtpsOnly').
guardrails.risk: FTP sends deployment credentials in clear text.
guardrails.policy: FTPS only should be required in App Service apps

guardrails.recommendation: Keep remote debugging disabled outside of short troubleshooting windows.
guardrails.risk: Remote debugging opens additional inbound ports on the worker.
guardrails.policy: App Service apps should have remote debugging turned off

environment.recommendation: Require multi-factor authentication for all users through Conditional Access.
environment.risk: Password-only accounts are easily phished or sprayed.
environment.policy: Accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be MFA enabled
Conditional Access should block legacy authentication

environment.recommendation: Use Privileged Identity Management for eligible, time-bound role activation.
environment.risk: Standing privileged access increases the impact of a compromised account.
environment.policy: Privileged roles should use just-in-time access

environment.recommendation: Keep subscription owners to a small, reviewed group (between 2 and 3).
environment.risk: Too many owners widens the privileged attack surface.
environment.policy: A maximum of 3 owners should be designated for your subscription

environment.recommendation: Enable Defender CSPM and the workload plans (Servers, Storage, Key Vault, Databases, Containers) that match your estate.
environment.risk: Threats and misconfigurations are not detected.
environment.policy: Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans should be enabled

environment.recommendation: Remove guest and external accounts from privileged roles and review access regularly.
environment.risk: External identities are outside your lifecycle and MFA controls.
environment.policy: Guest accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be removed

environment.recommendation: Prefer built-in least-privilege roles; avoid wildcard custom roles.
environment.risk: Custom wildcard roles silently grant owner-equivalent rights.
environment.policy: Custom subscription owner roles should not exist

environment.recommendation: Configure security contact details and alert notifications in Defender for Cloud.
environment.policy: Subscriptions should have a contact email address for security issues

environment.recommendation: Enforce tags such as environment, owner and cost-center with Azure Policy.
environment.risk: Untagged resources cannot be attributed, costed or cleaned up.

environment.recommendation: Restrict deployments to approved regions with Azure Policy.
environment.risk: Data residency obligations can be breached.

environment.recommendation: Assign the Microsoft cloud security benchmark policy initiative at management group scope.
environment.policy: Microsoft cloud security benchmark initiative should be assigned

environment.recommendation: Register only the resource providers you need and review preview features before enabling them.
environment.risk: Unreviewed preview features may not meet security and support requirements.
environment.policy: Resource providers should be registered deliberately
